name: Floors route → NOT-CLEAN (measured red): stamp the intermediate
description:
The not-clean intermediate, branch 1 of 2 (design R1, group 5). 'Not clean' = the attempt measured red (route.attempt.passed=false, incl. the fail-closed 'never measured' case) OR a structural floor rejected it (route.attempt.rejected=true). That is a DISJUNCTION, and the retry/escalate routes must AND it with the budget count — but a rule has ONE flat logic (never mixed AND/OR), so '(A or B) and count' is not one rule. This is the OR-collapse: two GUARDED pure-AND rules (this one on route.attempt.passed, 06e on route.attempt.rejected) each stamp a single-valued route.attempt.unclean='true', and the retry (06c)/escalate (06d) rules read that intermediate with pure-AND conditions.

WHY TWO GUARDED RULES rather than one logic:or rule: a rule's add_triple appends unconditionally and bumps the entity version (graph-ingest has no 'nothing-changed' skip on the ADD path, verified against beta.146), so a GUARDLESS rule whose trigger stays true would re-fire and re-append every rescan (unbounded churn). The route.attempt.unclean length_eq 0 self-extinguish guard makes each branch fire-once (a fresh developer loop L_n per attempt re-arms it) — but a guard is an AND condition, which cannot coexist with a logic:or over the signals. So the disjunction is split into two guarded AND rules. Both stamp the SAME single-valued route.attempt.unclean='true' (idempotent for the reader: 06c/06d read route.attempt.unclean eq 'true'); if both branches match (passed=false AND rejected=true) both fire ONCE, then the shared guard blocks re-fire — bounded, no churn.

TRIGGER = the developer loop L_n: route.attempt.passed eq "false" (required:false — the scalar exists only on a floors loop, so it fires only there and only when measured red) AND route.attempt.unclean length_eq 0 (the self-extinguish guard). Mutually exclusive with the advance route (06a requires route.attempt.passed=true).

G2: this fires no lifecycle transition and no spawn — it records the harness-derived not-clean verdict as a fact the retry/escalate RULES compose the route from. The route DECISION lives entirely in 06c/06d, never in Go.

metadata.station: route not_clean (measured red) — the OR-collapse branch 1 (R1, group 5)
metadata.or_collapse: the not-clean disjunction (route.attempt.passed=false OR route.attempt.rejected=true) is split into TWO GUARDED pure-AND rules (this + 06e) so each carries the route.attempt.unclean length_eq 0 self-extinguish guard — a guardless logic:or rule would re-fire and re-append unbounded (the ADD path bumps version with no nothing-changed skip). Both stamp the same single-valued route.attempt.unclean='true' the retry/escalate rules read.
metadata.self_extinguish: route.attempt.unclean length_eq 0 guard → fire-once; a fresh developer loop L_n per attempt re-arms it. Bounded even if both branches match (each fires once, then the guard blocks).
